definition: Advantageous means providing a benefit or an edge; favorable to one's interests.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word advantageous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know advantageous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Arriving a day early proved advantageous: the debate team got the quiet practice room and two full rehearsals before the judges ever appeared.
Convenient describes something that merely saves you a little effort, while advantageous means it actually improves your position or prospects.
Advantageous describes a real edge, but invaluable describes a benefit so great that success would be hard to imagine without it.

Favorable means leaning your way — favorable conditions, favorable reviews, a favorable wind. Advantageous is stronger and more concrete: something actually gives you a benefit or an edge over others. A favorable forecast merely helps your plans along; an advantageous contract measurably improves your position against rivals.

Beneficial means producing good or helpful effects, the way exercise is beneficial to health or rain is beneficial to crops. Advantageous adds a competitive angle: it gives one party an edge or a better position. Something can be beneficial to everyone at once, but advantageous implies someone gains ground on someone else.

A small furniture startup had to choose between two warehouses that cost the same to rent.
One sat beside the freight rail line; the other was twenty miles from any major route.
The founders chose the rail-side site, and within a year their shipping costs ran far below their competitors' and orders arrived days sooner.
The location proved advantageous in exactly the way the founders had hoped, giving the young company a genuine edge in a crowded market.
The rail-side warehouse gave the company a real benefit and an edge over its rivals, which is precisely what advantageous describes.

Advantageous often pairs with 'to' or 'for' plus whoever gains the edge (advantageous to the buyer, advantageous for early applicants).
It is about benefit, not ease: a merger can be advantageous even if carrying it out is exhausting, and an easy task can be advantageous to no one.

At the regional robotics meet, teams claimed pit tables on a first-come basis, and most grabbed whatever stood nearest the door.
Maya's team walked past the empty front row and took a cramped table beside the practice field instead, trading legroom for something better.
The choice looked odd, but it proved advantageous within an hour: her drivers could test between every match while rivals waited in a long corridor line.
By afternoon the team had logged three times as many practice runs as anyone else, and their robot's aim had visibly sharpened with each round.
